Subject: Request: security architecture overview for Dedicated/Private deployments

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. As part of Atlantic Bank's vendor risk review, our security team needs a concise architecture overview that focuses on two items we flagged:

1) Tenant scoping — how customer workloads are partitioned (logical vs physical) across Dedicated and Private deployment options and what guarantees we provide against cross-tenant data leakage.
2) Traffic governance and egress controls — how outbound traffic is restricted, per-tenant egress policies, and how those controls integrate with customer-managed networking (VPC/VPN).

Could you please send: a one-page narrative, a network diagram that includes control-plane/data-plane demarcation for both Dedicated and Private, and any short evidence snippets (ACL examples, egress rule templates) you can share? We'll bundle these in our SIG/SOC2 questionnaire submission.

We'd appreciate receiving this by EOD Thursday (May 28) so our risk team can review ahead of the steering committee. If anything is sensitive, mark it as such and we'll treat it under NDA.

Best,
Lauren Price
Senior InfoSec Manager — Third-Party Risk
Atlantic Bank

Hi all —

Working on this. Quick clarifications before we finalize the diagram and evidence pack:

1) "Tenant scoping" — do they want the behavioral guarantees (e.g., cryptographic separation of customer data at rest, KV cache scoping) or primarily network-level separation (VNets/subnets, host pools)? We'll include both if helpful but want the right emphasis.

2) Egress controls — we have two typical patterns to show:
  - Pattern A (Hosted/Dedicated hybrid): outbound egress proxied through a Redwood-managed egress gateway with per-account ACLs enforced at the gateway + prefix/KV cache rules. This is ideal when we manage the control plane and can provide managed egress.
  - Pattern B (Private/VPC-hosted): egress routes terminate in customer-managed NAT/GW; Redwood provides per-tenant security groups and a policy bundle (egress-policy-table.xlsx) that customers apply to their NAT/GW or firewall.

3) Evidence snippets — I will attach: network-diagram-v1.pdf (combined control/data demarcation), a sanitized ACL export (egress-policy-table.xlsx), and a short SOC2 Q&A excerpt (soc2-qna-digest.docx). All attachments will have redacted IPs for external circulation.

If Atlantic wants a more prescriptive template for firewall rules (lines to paste into Palo Alto/Checkpoint), we can add a second tab in the egress spreadsheet.

I'll aim to have the diagram + narrative by Wednesday EOD and the attachments packaged by Thu EOD.

Kimberly Park
Principal Security Architect — Redwood Inference
